Console.indexTroubleshootingTitle: What to do when indexing fails
Console.indexTroubleshootingStepFix: Read the failure reason and recommended action on the failed index card before clearing anything.
Console.indexTroubleshootingStepRestart: For a client or network interruption, reopen the project, reload the IDE window, or restart the LCE MCP client, then keep the project open.
Console.indexTroubleshootingStepKeepOpen: For model-service, server, quota, or unknown errors, select “Copy diagnostics” and send them to an administrator. These issues usually cannot be fixed on the user's computer.
Console.indexTroubleshootingStepCheck: After the cause is fixed, confirm that a new task moves from “Waiting for client upload” to upload/vector indexing and finally “Index ready”.
Console.indexTroubleshootingRetryNote: Refreshing this page or asking the Agent another question only checks state; it does not reliably restart a failed job. Reopen the project or restart the LCE MCP client.
Console.indexTroubleshootingCleanupNote: “Clear failure” only hides the failed task. It does not fix the cause, start a retry, or delete an existing usable index.

Console.indexRecoveryResetRoot: This cloud root uses the previous embedding space and cannot accept new writes. Select “Reset cloud index” to delete the repository/branch cloud root and Relay state, then restart the MCP client to rebuild it. Clearing only the failure record will not fix this error.
Console.indexRecoveryServiceRecovers: This is a remote index service or gateway failure. When service recovers, reload the IDE window or restart the LCE MCP client to start a new job.
Console.indexRecoveryFixProviderBilling: Top up the affected model service balance or switch to a working model configuration. Verify it, then restart the MCP client.
Console.indexRecoveryRetryLater: Wait for the provider rate-limit window, reduce concurrency if needed, then restart the MCP client to index again.
Console.indexRecoveryReduceRepository: Ignore generated files, dependencies, and large files, or split the repository to meet file-count and per-file size limits, then restart the MCP client.
Console.indexRecoveryWaitForQuotaReset: A current indexing client that remains running automatically creates a new sync after the server quota resets. If the client is closed or does not support automatic recovery, restart it after quota becomes available.
Console.indexRecoveryFixCredentials: Contact an administrator to verify the provider URL, API key, and model names. After it is fixed, reopen the project or restart the LCE MCP client.
Console.indexRecoveryContactAdmin: This issue cannot normally be fixed by an end user. Copy the diagnostics and contact an administrator, then reopen the project or restart the LCE MCP client after the service is fixed.
Console.indexRecoveryInspectLogs: Copy the diagnostics and contact an administrator; end users do not need to inspect server logs.

Home.itIndexesRepositoriesIntoStructuredSeman: . It helps MCP-compatible editors and coding agents understand the current project, locate problems, and assess the impact of changes.

Home.lceProvidesAReadyToUseCloud: LCE is ready to use as a cloud service. Create an account and add the configuration generated in the console to your IDE.
Home.combinesSemanticKeywordAndExactTermRetri: Describe a feature, problem, or goal to find relevant implementations without knowing function names, variable names, or file locations.
Home.connectsWorkflowsAcrossFilesModulesAndPr: Connects one workflow across files, modules, and projects so agents understand the full implementation instead of isolated snippets.
Home.resultsIncludeFilePathsSymbolsAndExact: Returns file paths, symbols, and accurate line ranges so agents can go directly to the code that matters.
Home.processesOnlyAddedAndChangedFilesRemoves: Keeps project context current as code is added, changed, or deleted without repeatedly processing the whole project from scratch.
Home.readsGitStatusBranchesDiffsHistoryAndBla: Reads working tree status, branch differences, commit history, and line-level origins so agents can understand how code evolved and the context behind changes.
Home.supportsTypescriptJavascriptPythonGoRust: Supports TypeScript/JavaScript, Python, Go, Rust, Java, C/C++, C#, PHP, Swift, Kotlin, and common configuration and documentation files.
Home.buildsACodeGraphFromAstAnd: Shows definitions, references, callers, callees, and dependencies so agents can understand how code connects.
Home.identifiesCallersDependentModulesAffecte: Identifies callers, dependent modules, affected tests, and regression risks before code is changed.
Home.combinesNaturalLanguageRetrievalExactTer: Uses the reported behavior to narrow down failure paths, related implementations, and the likely impact area.
Home.enhancesNaturalLanguageCodingRequestsWit: Uses the current project to turn a natural-language task into clearer goals, requirements, constraints, relevant code, and verification steps.
Home.promptEnhancementUsageIntro: Before a complex task begins, the agent can use the current repository to clarify scope, identify relevant code, and prepare a verification plan. The enhanced brief supplements the original request without replacing or rewriting it.
Home.promptEnhancementAskDescription: Describe the problem and include any known symbols, file names, or error codes as useful leads.
Home.promptEnhancementAgentCallsDescription: The agent calls codebase_enhance_prompt, retrieves evidence from the current index, and produces a structured implementation brief.
Home.promptEnhancementContinueDescription: Review the goals, constraints, code references, and verification steps before asking the agent to continue.
Home.promptEnhancementExample: Use codebase_enhance_prompt first to clarify the task boundaries and verification plan from the current repository, then implement the result without changing my original requirements: fix authentication timeout handling and add regression tests. Relevant leads: AuthService, sessionTTL.
Home.promptEnhancementAvailability: An administrator must enable a prompt-enhancement model under Model Management. Until then, the agent will state that this capability is unavailable.
Home.mcpToolsIntro: The default npx connection provides these six tools.
Home.withoutNpmClientToolWarning: The default npx configuration downloads and runs @anmezing/lce-cloud automatically, with no global install required. The client watches local changes, triggers incremental synchronization, keeps the current branch view up to date, and provides Git context and change review.
Home.npmClientModeDescription: Provides all six tools. The client watches file changes, triggers incremental synchronization, keeps the current branch view up to date, and adds index progress, Git context, and change review.
Home.signUpAndGetAnApiKey: Sign up and get an API key
Home.openTheConsoleAndGenerateAnApi: Open the console and generate an API key under API Keys.
Home.addTheMcpConfigurationToYourIde: Open Setup Guide in the console, choose generic JSON or TOML as required by your MCP client, and add the generated configuration to your editor, IDE, or coding agent.
Home.globalInstallationAvoidsRepeatedPackageR: A global installation avoids resolving or downloading the npm package at startup, so launches are faster and more reliable. You can still use the generated npx configuration without installing globally; while running, it provides the same file watching, incremental indexing, and branch-view synchronization.
Home.theDefaultNpxConfigurationNeedsNoInstall: . You can also keep the default npx configuration; both modes provide file watching, incremental indexing, and branch-view synchronization.
Home.makeLceTheAgentSFirstChoice: Make LCE the agent's first choice
Home.addingAnMcpServerDoesNotGuarantee: Adding an MCP server does not guarantee the agent will use it. Add this rule to CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, or .cursor/rules in the project root so the agent uses LCE before grep, rg, or browsing files. You can copy it from Setup Guide:
Home.afterSetupYourCodingAgentCanCall: Once configured, ask your agent to find and understand code, analyze relationships and change impact, or refine a task using the current project.
Home.retrievalEngineItDoesNotEditCode: code context service. It gives agents information but does not edit code, run tests, or create pull requests on its own.
Home.retrievalQualityDependsOnIndexCoverageFi: LCE can only understand files included in the project context; excluded files do not appear in results.
Home.inCloudModeIndexingAndRetrievalBoth: In Cloud mode, indexing and retrieval both run in the cloud.
Home.gitStatusHistoryBlameAndChangeReview: Git status, history, blame, and change review run locally and are not sent to the cloud.
Home.typescriptJavascriptSymbolGraphsPreferBo: TypeScript/JavaScript symbol graphs prefer bounded compiler projects. Files outside the compilation budget fall back to AST or heuristic facts with coverage and confidence labels.
Home.theServerRejectsEnvFilesKeysBinaries: LCE follows Git ignore rules and excludes common key files, dependencies, build output, and binaries. Review ordinary source files for hard-coded sensitive values before use.
